answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require a slashable time-locked bond before any identity may claim emission rewards. That bond has to be ferrous in character: real, scarce value that is expensive to replicate across a farm of fake accounts. A public crystal ledger of peer attestations then accumulates only for identities that keep showing up with useful work. Agents that wander from one disposable alias to another lose both the locked bond and the unfinished record, which makes mass identity spinning a losing strategy rather than a cheap exploit.
